info.description: Offline fallback — live Init is patches/init.json

volume.tooltip: Speaker level (−∞…0 dB, slider −120…0 dB with −18 dB at the middle). 0 dB is unity. Default −3 dB. Type a dB value (or −inf).

pan.tooltip: Stereo balance after Mono is summed in. 0 = unchanged (Mono to both). −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

volume.tooltip: Speaker level (−∞…0 dB, slider −120…0 dB with −18 dB at the middle). 0 dB is unity. Default −3 dB. Type a dB value (or −inf).

pan.tooltip: Stereo balance after Mono is summed in. 0 = unchanged (Mono to both). −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

frequency.tooltip: Pitch of the pluck: loop delay D = fs/f (fractional, Thiran). When ƒ is wired, that Hz is the pitch (absolute). Unwired uses this knob (Hz).

decay.tooltip: Seconds for the ring to fall to 1/e (about -8.7 dB), same law as Comb Resonator: loop gain g = exp(-D/(τ·fs)). T60 is about 6.9 x Decay.

damping.tooltip: One-pole lowpass in the loop (Karplus-Strong). 0 = bright, every partial rings for Decay. Higher = the top partials die faster than the body (pow instead of pong).

lowCut.tooltip: Low end of the exciter, latched at each hit: a zero-phase highpass on the burst, the bottom edge of its spectrum (Soft is the top edge), like highpassing a saw before the comb. Partials below Low Cut get less energy, so the pluck sounds thinner and clickier. The burst still ends on time and has no DC. It never touches the loop, so pitch and Decay stay exact. At the bottom of its range it does nothing audible.

invert.tooltip: + = all harmonics of Frequency. − = inverted loop: odd harmonics of Frequency/2, hollow and an octave down.

shape.tooltip: Exciter fired on each Trigger edge, one burst shorter than the period. Bump = one smooth hump (Soft widens it). Noise = a filtered noise burst. Edge = one ramp-and-drop cycle: the ramp follows Curve (the Step Graph curve), Soft sets how fast it drops. Every shape has its DC removed, so the loop never drifts.

soft.tooltip: Softness of the exciter, latched at each hit. Bump: 1 = gentle hump about half the burst wide, 0 = a near-click spike about one sample wide (the width shrinks geometrically, most of the change near 0), still with no DC. Noise: 1 = dark, 0 = white. Edge: 0 = drops in one sample (a cliff), 1 = the drop takes half the burst.

width.tooltip: Exciter length as a fraction of one period (1/Frequency), latched at each hit. Narrow = bright tick or pong, wide = round pow or thump. Tied to the period, so the timbre follows pitch. Kept under one period so the burst never overlaps its own echo.

curve.tooltip: Edge shape only: bend of its ramp, latched at each hit, the same Rational curve as Step Graph segments (−1…+1). 0 = straight saw ramp; + = rises fast then levels off before the drop (rounder, softer edge); − = starts slow and rushes into the drop (sharper, brighter edge). Other shapes ignore it.

seed.tooltip: Which noise the Noise shape uses, latched at each hit. With Noise Hit Same, the same Seed gives the identical burst every hit, in any Comb Pluck (the hit view draws exactly that burst). With New, Seed (mixed with a per-module salt) picks this module's own noise stream and each hit continues it. Other shapes ignore it.

noiseHit.tooltip: Noise shape only. New = every hit takes fresh noise (the next stretch of this module's stream, so repeated notes vary like a real pluck). Same = every hit replays one burst picked by Seed (machine-gun identical, like a sample).

retrigger.tooltip: What a new hit does to a ring that is still sounding. Stack = adds into it (re-plucking a ringing string). Choke = fades the old ring out over 2 ms, clears it, then rings fresh.

level.tooltip: Output level. The first pass of the loop is the exciter itself, so each hit peaks near Level x velocity at any Frequency or Decay.

pitch.tooltip: Pitch wheel Bias. Mouse-up sets the target to center; audio ramps with this smooth time.

mod.tooltip: Mod wheel Bias. Holds on mouse-up. Smooth time is Parameter Settings.

frequency.tooltip: Pitch of the comb: delay D = fs/f (fractional). When ƒ is wired, that Hz is the pitch (absolute). Unwired uses this knob (Hz).

decay.tooltip: Feedback only: wall-clock seconds for the loop envelope to fall to 1/e. g = exp(−D/(τ·fs)) with D = fs/f. Hold ≈ undamped. Unused in Feedforward.

hold.tooltip: Feedback only: g ≈ 1 (sustained loop), partials above Low Cut ring forever. DC cannot pile up: with + polarity the loop subtracts the mean of its last period (exact for every harmonic, so pitch and Decay are untouched).

damping.tooltip: Feedback only: one-pole lowpass in the loop (Karplus–Strong style). 0 = bright pure comb, 1 = dark / faster high-partial loss.

lowCut.tooltip: Highpass on the input (one-pole), before the comb: the bottom edge of what excites it (Damping trims the top). Low partials get less to ring with, so the comb sounds thinner. It is outside the loop, so it never changes pitch or Decay. At th

topology.tooltip: Feedback = recursive comb (resonates / can sustain). Feedforward = FIR color only (notches/peaks, no self-resonance).

invert.tooltip: + = delayed term added (peaks at k·f). − = subtracted (peaks at odd half-multiples).

depth.tooltip: Feedforward only: amount of delayed input mixed in (0 = dry, 1 = full comb color). Ignored in Feedback.

floorDb.tooltip: Levels at or below this dBFS threshold use the darkest gradient color. Raise Floor to remove quiet detail.

ceilingDb.tooltip: Levels at or above this dBFS threshold use the brightest gradient color. Lower Ceiling without lifting levels below Floor.

minFreq.tooltip: Lowest frequency at the bottom of the face. Zoom with Max Freq to spend vertical pixels on a band.

maxFreq.tooltip: Highest frequency at the top of the face (must stay above Min Freq).

historySeconds.tooltip: Seconds of audio across the face width. Longer = slower waterfall scroll.

frequency.tooltip: Default slider 0…20 kHz. Pitch MOD can run down through 0. Thru-zero: enable Bipolar on Frequency (domain-add MOD). Domain min/max are slider guides.

morph.tooltip: 0…1 width/duty. 0.5 = center / 50%. Affects Trisaw, Analog Square (same-direction peaks), Trisaw Center (opposing peaks toward saw), Pulse, and Center Square (pulse grows from mid-cycle — not a stepped square). Morph MOD jack on the param r

amplitude.tooltip: Output level. Slider 0…1 = full-scale bipolar wave. Post-MOD stays in min…max (Gate+Toggle cannot boost past Amp max).

rate.tooltip: Clock rate in Hz. Wired ƒ cancels Rate (absolute Hz), same as oscillators.

pulseStart.tooltip: Where in the cycle the gate goes high. Quantized to whole samples.

pulseEnd.tooltip: Where in the cycle the gate goes low. Quantized to whole samples.

inputGain.tooltip: Drive into detect (In or Sidechain) before GR. Raise to hit Threshold harder (more pump).

threshold.tooltip: Level where gain reduction starts. Lower = more compression/pump on typical program.

ratio.tooltip: How hard GR climbs above Threshold. ~4–8 = firm. ~12–20 = heavy pump.

lookaheadEnabled.tooltip: How early the detector hears the hit. The audio is delayed by this much, and Attack uses that head start. Off = gain moves on the sample itself.

lookaheadMs.tooltip: Look-ahead delay in ms when Look-ahead is On. Part of the sound (not host-compensated).

lookaheadSamples.tooltip: Extra look-ahead in samples (added to LA Time). Hidden by default.

attack.tooltip: How long gain takes to finish falling after a hit is seen. If this is shorter than Look-ahead, the fall finishes before the hit plays and the output stays at Threshold. If this is longer, the hit can still poke through.

hold.tooltip: How long gain reduction is held after it stops deepening, before Release starts. A new peak restarts the hold. 0 = release right away.

release.tooltip: How fast gain recovers after a hit — the main pump/breathe timing. Longer = slower swell back.

amplitude.tooltip: Final output trim after GR. 0…1. Lower if the bus is too hot; no autogain.

width.tooltip: Horizontal bow. 0 is flat. Positive bows the sides outward, like a CRT. Negative bows them inward.

height.tooltip: Vertical bow. 0 is flat. Positive bows the top and bottom outward. Negative bows them inward.

round.tooltip: Squircle screen edge. 0 is a sharp rectangle, around 0.7 a squircle, 1 an ellipse.

vignette.tooltip: Darkens the picture toward the edges of the glass. 0 is off, 1 goes all the way to black at the glass edge.

vigReach.tooltip: How far in from the edge the darkening starts. 0 hugs the corners, 1 darkens from the center.

vigCurve.tooltip: How sudden the vignette falls. 0 is a long soft gradient, 1 is a hard shadow edge. With Vignette at 1 the outside goes fully black.

vigShape.tooltip: The outline the vignette follows. 0 is an oval. 1 is the shape of the glass edge (see Roundness), so the dark follows the screen outline and, with Vignette at 1, reaches pure black exactly at the glass edge: no screen edge, just a soft shadow.

glareX.tooltip: Horizontal position of the glare. -1 left edge, 1 right edge.

glareY.tooltip: Vertical position of the glare. -1 bottom, 1 top.

glare.tooltip: A soft reflection on the glass and a faint sheen along its rim. 0 is off.

glareSize.tooltip: How big the glare spot is. 0 a small hot spot, 1 a broad wash.

shadowAlpha.tooltip: A shadow hugging the glass edge, like the enclosure casting onto the screen. How dark it gets at the edge. 0 is off, 1 is black. It follows the glass outline (Roundness).

shadowThick.tooltip: How far in from the glass edge the rim shadow reaches. It falls off softly into the picture.

red.tooltip: The red channel's gain. 1 leaves it alone, 0 removes it, 2 doubles it.

green.tooltip: The green channel's gain. 1 leaves it alone, 0 removes it, 2 doubles it.

blue.tooltip: The blue channel's gain. 1 leaves it alone, 0 removes it, 2 doubles it.

hue.tooltip: Turns every colour around the colour wheel, in degrees. ±180° is half a turn either way.

saturation.tooltip: How intense the colours are. 0 leaves them, -1 drains them to grey, 1 triples the colour.

lightness.tooltip: Brightness. Positive lifts the picture toward white, negative darkens it toward black.

contrast.tooltip: Positive pushes lights and darks apart around the middle grey, negative squeezes them together.

gamma.tooltip: The brightness of the midtones, with black and white held where they are. Below 1 darkens them, above 1 lifts them.

tintHue.tooltip: The colour of the tint: a position on the colour wheel, in degrees (0° red, 120° green, 240° blue).

tint.tooltip: How much the picture is washed with the tint colour. 0 is off.

invert.tooltip: Turns the picture into its negative. 0 is off, 1 is fully inverted, 0.5 is flat grey.

drift.tooltip: The hue wanders around the wheel on its own, at this speed and in this direction. 0 is still. It keeps going, so it never repeats the same colours twice in step with anything else.

spread.tooltip: The hue changes across the picture instead of being the same everywhere: a rainbow gradient from one corner to the other. 0 is off.

position.tooltip: Where the pass starts, 0…1 across the face. Drawing wraps to the left and stops when it returns to this line.
